secondary.application: Compare each per-task candidate median against control. A strictly greater ratio flags a regression; candidate positive against control zero flags without division. Flags prevent blanket efficiency claims and require route analysis. They do not automatically discard improved functional coverage.

decision_rule.zero_comparator: For primary ratio gates, both zero passes; positive candidate against zero control fails.
decision_rule.interpretation: Correctness precedes cost. Retain each valid failure, incomplete run, recovery and exhausted budget in all-run totals. Report per-task medians/ranges, paired directions and totals. These practical diagnostic gates do not establish statistical equivalence. Passing nonregression limits alone is not a speedup. Treat this as a combined help package; do not attribute effects to individual sentences. This correction reruns only task 12, whose median uncached input exceeded its bound in agent-regression-2026-10-24-v1; overall gates apply to these 8 sessions, and its total calls may exceed the control's by one, as for every single-task correction since 2026-10-22.
decision_rule.stopping: Run only the first frozen 8 sessions. Never pool prior trials, replace valid failures or add repetitions. A correction requires a new candidate and frozen protocol before further trials. Invalid context, unsupported actual model/effort, missing/corrupt telemetry or fixture/instrumentation failures make affected evidence inadmissible; do not silently substitute trials.

integrity: Freeze exact protocol, schedule, tasks, expected artifacts/interpretations, native binary hashes and each arm source provenance before launching any explorer. Keep preparation repository snapshot provenance separate from prebuilt-binary source declarations. At most three pairs run concurrently and arms run sequentially inside each pair. Preserve identical inputs, locale, terminal/width behavior, isolated personal defaults and budgets across arms. Independent fresh MEDIUM agents receive no repository documentation, prior answers, telemetry or outside-scratch access.
review: Independently grade artifacts and final answers with condition/resource labels concealed; audit actual model/effort, initial context, final cumulative counters, isolation, order, hashes and fixture integrity. Missing required work is incomplete; corrected mistakes may pass but retain recovery cost. Do not silently repair artifacts.
telemetry: Record agent-facing calls, shell executions, CLI invocations, uncached input (input minus cached), cached input, output including reasoning without double counting, guide/schema retrievals and final-delivery duration separately. Evaluator/reviewer work is excluded. The duration field uses the existing harness elapsed-through-completion/copying measurement, not exact native final-message latency.
evidence: Retain raw sessions and account/framework context only in Git-ignored docs/research/local/agent-explorability. Public results contain portable synthetic summaries and provenance, never raw session/account content.

task_roles.12: Configuration of a Rust project whose test kinds and scripts need categories the agent names

candidate_change: The categories guide shortened from 10,009 to 5,932 bytes: tighter descriptions, fewer replaced names and worked cases, and conventions that link the configure guide; it now keeps names the owner chose or a policy declares and allows custom names that keep a distinction a reference row would merge. Vocabulary and order are unchanged.
hypothesis: In the first run, agents fetched the 10 KB guide in one batch with the configure guide and schema, overflowed the harness output cap and fetched it again; a guide about half that size should fit the batch and keep the median within 110% of the control's.
coverage_boundary: Evaluate only these eight freshly paired task-12 sessions. Do not pool the first run's trials into any correctness rate, median, total or gate. Category names are a diagnostic: report agreement with the reference names and between runs per arm, never as a gate.
